Pulmonary embolism or aortic dissection are less likely given stable oxygenation, lack of tachycardia >100, and no focal exam/ECG findings, though these would be considered if the clinical picture changes.

Overall, after integrating the emotional precipitant, symptom pattern, and currently normal cardiac testing, an acute panic (anxiety) attack is the single most likely diagnosis right now, with continued appropriate rule‑out of ACS (serial troponins) as planned.

[DIAGNOSIS]
Acute panic (anxiety) attack.
